## Context

`tests/interfaces/store/test_event_append_index_lock.py::test_contended_index_lock_cleared_during_backoff_succeeds` failed on the `pytest (macos-latest, py3.13)` leg of the Gerrit Verified gate (run 31338947918, change 1575), and was reported on change 1574 in the same hour. Neither change touches `src/rebar/_store`. On run 31338947918 the three Linux legs passed the identical tree; only macOS failed, and that leg took 23m24s against ~12m for each Linux leg.

    rebar._store.event_append.StoreError: Error: git commit failed while holding lock:
    fatal: unable to write new index file

## ROOT CAUSE — PROVEN (test-timing; reproduced locally with the exact CI error string)

The test deletes **git's own real `index.lock`** out from under the `git commit` it is testing.

`stage_and_commit` runs under the exclusive store write lock, so `_git_add`/`_git_commit`
(`src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`) pass `force_reclaim=True` into
`gitutil._with_index_lock_retry`. Under `force=True` the age gate is bypassed, so the planted
young lock is force-reclaimed on the FIRST retry rather than blocking for long:

- t=0    the test plants a young `index.lock` and arms `threading.Timer(0.4, ...)`
- t≈0    `git add` attempt 1 fails on the lock; `_reclaim_if_stale_index_lock(force=True)` removes the planted lock
- t≈0.2  `git add` attempt 2 succeeds
- t≈0.2+ `git commit` runs and creates git's OWN REAL `index.lock`
- t=0.4  the Timer fires and unlinks **whatever lock exists** — on a slow runner, git's real one, mid-commit
- git's `commit_locked_index` rename fails: `fatal: unable to write new index file`

The timer body is `lambda: lock.exists() and lock.unlink()` — no identity check, so it cannot
distinguish the planted lock from git's. On a fast machine `git commit` finishes before t=0.4;
on the slow macOS leg it is still holding its lock.

Local reproduction (test shape preserved, backoff widened so the timer lands inside `git commit`):

    FAIL StoreError: Error: git commit failed while holding lock:
         fatal: unable to write new index file   timer_deleted_at=[0.4314896250143647]

RULED OUT:
- **Runner resource exhaustion** — all failing job logs across the cited runs grep clean for
  `No space` / `ENOSPC` / `Cannot allocate` / runner warnings (zero hits). Slowness is real but
  is an amplifier of the window above, not the cause.
- **A real backoff race** — the production path is correct throughout: it force-reclaims the
  orphan, retries, and succeeds. No product change is warranted.
- **Lock-retry classification** — `unable to write new index file` is correctly absent from
  `_is_git_lock_error`; it is a genuine write failure and must not be retried blindly.

## Plan

Replace the wall-clock `threading.Timer` release with the seam `gitutil` already ships for
exactly this purpose: `_retry_probe`, documented as "a deterministic alternative to timer-based
lock release". It fires after every attempt inside `_with_index_lock_retry`, so the test can
release the planted lock **only after the first failure is confirmed** — no wall clock, and no
way to delete a lock git owns. Test-only change; no production behavior is modified.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `test_contended_index_lock_cleared_during_backoff_succeeds` no longer uses a wall-clock
      timer to release the planted lock, so it can never unlink a lock held by the `git add`/
      `git commit` under test.
- [ ] The test still proves what it did before: a CONTENDED (young, live-peer) `index.lock`
      that is released mid-retry is ridden out and the write succeeds (`rc == 0` and the
      COMMENT event is committed).
- [ ] The lock release is driven by an observed retry attempt (`gitutil._retry_probe`), not by
      elapsed time, so the test is insensitive to runner speed.
- [ ] The test passes repeatedly under load locally (>= 50 consecutive runs, and under `-n 4`
      xdist) with no timing-dependent failures.
- [ ] No file under `src/rebar/` is modified by this change.
